n: Ammon speaks to his brothers with overflowing joy: when they left Zarahemla, could they have imagined such blessings?

f.w: how great reason have we to rejoice
f.g: This chapter is often called Ammon’s “psalm of praise.”

n: He asks them to name the great blessings God has given.

f.g: A teaching question that leads into his answer.

n: He answers: the Lamanites were in the darkest abyss, but many now see God’s marvelous light — and the missionaries were God’s instruments in this work.

f.w: instruments in the hands of God

n: Thousands now rejoice in God’s fold.
Harvest imagery: the field was ripe, they thrust in the sickle and reaped all day — look at the sheaves! They will be stored safely in the barns.
These converts won’t be beaten down by the storms of the last day; they will be safely gathered where no storm or enemy wind can reach them.
They belong to the Lord of the harvest, who will raise them up at the last day.
Ammon bursts into praise: let us sing and give thanks to God, who works righteousness forever.

f.w: let us sing to his praise

n: If they hadn’t come, these beloved Lamanite brothers would still hate them and be strangers to God.
Aaron cautions Ammon that his joy might be turning into boasting.
Ammon clarifies: he boasts not in his own strength or wisdom; his heart is simply full of joy in God.

f.w: my heart is brim with joy

n: He knows he is nothing and weak in himself; he boasts only of God, in whose strength he can do all things.

f.w: I know that I am nothing
in his strength I can do all things

n: Thousands have been freed from hell’s pains and now sing redeeming love through the power of God’s word.
We should praise God forever — the Most High, who loosed our brothers from hell’s chains.
Once surrounded by darkness, they are now surrounded by God’s light and the matchless bounty of his love.

f.w: the matchless bounty of his love

n: Who can glory too much in the Lord? Ammon cannot express even the smallest part of what he feels.

f.w: I cannot say the smallest part which I feel

n: Who would have thought God would rescue us from our awful, sinful state? Ammon remembers his own past.
They had once gone out in anger, threatening to destroy God’s church.
Why didn’t God let the sword of justice fall on them?
Ammon’s soul almost recoils at the thought. Instead of justice, God mercifully carried them over the gulf of death and misery to salvation.
No “natural man” — one who is unrepentant and worldly — understands these things; only the penitent do.
To those who repent, have faith, do good, and pray constantly, God reveals his mysteries and gives power to bring thousands to repentance.
Ammon recalls how people in Zarahemla laughed when they announced their mission.
Their critics doubted the Lamanites, a people known for bloodshed and wickedness, could ever be converted.
Some even proposed war to wipe them out.

f.g: War, not missionary work, was the popular solution.

n: But the brothers came not to destroy but to save even a few souls.

f.w: save some few of their souls

n: When discouraged and ready to quit, the Lord comforted them and promised success if they endured patiently.
They endured every hardship, going house to house and relying on the mercy of others — and more importantly on God’s mercy.
They taught in homes, streets, hills, temples, and synagogues — and were mocked, spat on, struck, stoned, bound, and jailed, yet God delivered them.
They endured it all hoping to save even one soul, thinking that would make their joy full.
Now they see the fruits: not a few, but many. The converts’ love proves their sincerity.
These converts would rather die than kill even an enemy, and buried their weapons out of love.

f.w: buried their weapons of war deep in the earth

n: Has there ever been such love in the land? Not even among the Nephites.
The Nephites would fight; these converts laid down their lives out of love and hatred of sin, and are with God.
No one since the world began has had more reason to rejoice. Ammon boasts in God — all-powerful, all-wise, and merciful to the repentant.
If this is boasting, so be it — God is his life, light, joy, salvation, and redemption. God has remembered this branch of Israel broken off in a strange land.

f.w: a branch of the tree of Israel

n: Ammon’s conclusion: God is mindful of every people in every land; his mercy covers the whole earth.

f.w: God is mindful of every people
